doc.title: Ray Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, AZ, April 16, 2000

chapter: Reflections on playing and jazz today
title: Musicians he never recorded with; Cannonball Adderley
summary: Brown names Miles, Dexter Gordon and Erroll Garner as people he played with but never recorded, and praises Cannonball and Ernie Wilkins.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Out of the unbelievable list of people that you’ve played with, or that have played with you, is there anybody you felt like you missed along the way?
Yeah. That you could have maybe enjoyed doing an album with?

There are a couple of people I didn’t record with but I played with them. I never recorded with Miles and I never recorded with Dexter Gordon. I never recorded with Eroll Garner. © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

I grew up with him. But I mean I played with him many times. I played with Miles, he played in Dizzy’s big band. I played with Dexter but I didn’t record. There’s maybe a half a dozen people that I never recorded with, but just about everybody I’ve played with somewhere.
I love these Cannonball records by the way.
Oh yeah. He was such a marvelous player.
Gee wasn’t he great? And Ernie Wilkins arrangements were top.
